capabilities: prototype: fixed allowlist of static HTTP canary endpoints
prototype: loopback-only IPv4 binding by default; non-loopback binding requires explicit opt-in
prototype: unknown paths are not recorded and configured paths return static 404/405 responses
prototype: minimal versioned JSONL events store only a truncated source prefix (/24 IPv4 or /64 IPv6) and omit full source address, raw path, query, headers, cookies, credentials, and request bodies
prototype: append-only event writes with mode 0600 and a 64 MiB size limit
prototype: STIX 2.1 bundle export using optional pinned stix2 library
prototype: no outbound scanning, proxying, arbitrary file serving, authentication, or command execution
negative_scope: fabricated or simulated live operational evidence

platforms.notes: Deterministic loopback HTTP, JSONL, privacy, schema, and STIX parsing tests run in CI.

platforms.target: Other POSIX hosts and non-loopback deployments
platforms.notes: Not yet tested outside the recorded Ubuntu CI environment; wider binding requires explicit operator opt-in.

runtime: Python standard library for HTTP service and JSONL event capture
optional: jsonschema==4.23.0 for development and CI validation

interfaces: Versioned event record schema: schemas/event.schema.json v1.0
STIX 2.1 bundle export containing sensor identity, ipv4-addr/ipv6-addr source prefix, network-traffic, observed-data, and note objects

claims.claim: Loopback HTTP canary routes, privacy boundaries, append-only JSONL handling, and event schema validation pass deterministic tests on Python 3.9 through 3.13 on Ubuntu 24.04.
STIX 2.1 bundles generated from fixture events parse successfully with stix2 3.0.1; no actor attribution objects are emitted.
Public exposure, non-loopback deployment, production hardening, and external operational observations.
The event schema and compatibility manifest validate against their declared Draft 2020-12 schemas; the CLI entry point is available.
